_meta.indication: FARYDAK, a histone deacetylase inhibitor, in combination with bortezomib and dexamethasone, is indicated for the treatment of patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least 2 prior regimens, including bortezomib and an immunomodulatory agent; approved under accelerated approval based on progression-free survival.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study of panobinostat in combination with bortezomib and dexamethasone versus placebo plus bortezomib and dexamethasone.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with relapsed multiple myeloma who had received 1 to 3 prior lines of therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival (PFS) using modified EBMT criteria, as assessed by the investigators.
pivotal_trials.result: In the overall population, median PFS 12 months vs 8.1 months [HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.52, 0.76)]. Approval was based on a prespecified subgroup of 193 patients with prior bortezomib and an immunomodulatory agent: median PFS 10.6 months vs 5.8 months [HR 0.52 (0.36, 0.76)]. Overall survival was not statistically different.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥20%) are diarrhea, fatigue, nausea, peripheral edema, decreased appetite, pyrexia, and vomiting. Diarrhea of any grade occurred in 68% (severe 25%) vs 42% in control; nausea 36% vs 21%. Serious toxicities include severe/fatal cardiac ischemic events, arrhythmias (any grade 12% vs 5%), fatal and serious hemorrhage, and myelosuppression (including severe thrombocytopenia, neutropenia and anemia).
target_moa: Panobinostat is a small molecule histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor active against HDAC isoforms in class I, II and IV at low nanomolar concentrations, causing accumulation of acetylated histones and non-histone proteins, apoptosis and cell cycle arrest, including in human multiple myeloma cells.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: FATAL AND SERIOUS TOXICITIES: SEVERE DIARRHEA AND CARDIAC TOXICITIES. Severe diarrhea occurred in 25% of FARYDAK treated patients. Severe and fatal cardiac ischemic events, severe arrhythmias, and ECG changes have occurred.

rems.type: A REMS consisting of a communication plan and a timetable for submission of assessments was approved; it must be fully operational before introduction into interstate commerce.

advisory_committee.vote: Presented to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee on November 6, 2014; the committee was asked whether the benefit outweighed the risks for patients with relapsed multiple myeloma, and five of seven committee members voted “No” and two voted “Yes”.
